text:
jessica (PM): ok team — quick thread to align on how we sequence the next model onboard wave. I think the usual RICE table isn't capturing the 'customer journey touchpoint' priority we keep seeing from sales :thinking:

jessica (PM): proposal: add a lightweight lane system (Frontline, Batch, Specialty) that maps to routing + SLAs. Score = RICE * lane_weight. Lane weight defaults: Frontline=1.5, Batch=0.8, Specialty=1.1. Thoughts?

mira (ML): curious why multiply vs add. Multiplying amplifies impact but also exaggerates low-confidence R scores. can we make the lane weight bounded and add an uncertainty penalty instead?

jessica (PM): fair — I like a small uncertainty penalty. idea: Score = RICE * lane_weight - UncertaintyFactor (0-20). keeps high-impact but risky models from jumping the queue.

sam (infra): operational note — Frontline lane implies strict latency SLOs (p99 < 250ms on hosted), must pass perf harness. If we tag a model Frontline we need a clear perf checklist.

leo (tech-ops): agreed. also add a Dedicated/Private readiness flag. Some customers ask for a model but will only adopt if it can run on Dedicated or VPC. That affects rollout cost/time.

anya (product-ops): from rollout perspective we should capture three launch gates in the doc: 1) Compatibility (model converts/quantizes), 2) Perf (latency/cost benchmarks), 3) Quality (evals on customer prompts). all required for Frontline.

mira (ML): quick sketch of gating thresholds for Quality: automatic evals (BLEU/EM/whatever) plus a small human eval sample. propose: automated pass rate >= 92% on core suite OR human rating >= 4/5 on 50 examples.

jessica (PM): that sounds actionable. can we add a simple RICE calc example in-thread?

mira (ML): sure — example for a popular open model request from 2 mid-market customers:
```
Reach = 2000 monthly requests
Impact = 4 (scale 1-5)
Confidence = 0.7
Effort = 3 (engineer-weeks)
RICE = (2000 * 4 * 0.7) / 3 = ~1867
Lane: Frontline => lane_weight=1.5, UncertaintyFactor=15 => Score ~ 2790 - 15 = 2775
```

sam (infra): numbers look fine but we should normalize Reach (e.g., per 1k requests) so big customers don't always dominate. maybe use log(Reach) in score.

jessica (PM): good call. make Reach = log10(requests + 1) * 1000 to keep scale comparable. update after lunch.

leo (tech-ops): practical constraint — some models can't be quantized without quality loss we observed. that becomes a binary blocker for Dedicated. Should we encode a "quantization feasibility" check as early in the intake form?

anya (product-ops): yes — intake form change. two checkbox fields: "quantizable (has 8-bit profile)" and "private-friendly (no external-reqs)". Intake auto-scores those and flags workstreams for infra/ML.

mira (ML): also want a small eval harness addition: a quick latency/cost sampler that runs sequence lengths 32/128/512 and returns tokens/sec and per-token cost estimate. That will speed gating.

sam (infra): we have a toy script for that in infra playground. i'll turn it into a CI job that runs on model upload. tag @dev-bot to create ticket.

dev-bot: created ticket INFRA-4723: "model perf CI job for intake sampler" assigned to sam. ETA 5d. :white_check_mark:

jessica (PM): next: sequencing mechanics. propose quarterly cadence with an emergency lane for security/customer-urgent models. The emergency lane bypasses normal wait but requires a dedicated rollout owner and 2x monitoring retention for first week.

leo (tech-ops): add automatic rollback thresholds: error rate > 2% OR latency p99 > SLO * 1.5 triggers immediate rollback to fallback model.

anya (product-ops): ops: we need a simple A/B template for canarying new models vs current default. I'll draft a 2-step: 5% traffic for 24h, check perf+quality, then 25% for 48h, then ramp. keep it configurable per-customer though.

mira (ML): one more tradeoff: smaller models with quantization often win cost but sometimes fail edge-case quality. Should we prefer model variants (small/large) in catalog entries and surface tradeoffs to customers?

jessica (PM): yes — catalog entry must include: variant tags, recommended lanes, quantization notes, sample eval summaries, and example prompts where model fails. Transparency helps sales and SREs.

sam (infra): final ask — let's add a perf budget column to the catalog: expected tokens/sec and cost-per-1k tokens on Standard and Dedicated. that helps routing decisions.

jessica (PM): thanks all. next steps: I'll update the intake form and scoring doc, @mira will draft the quality thresholds, @sam will create the perf CI job ticket (thanks bot), @anya will add the A/B template. reconvene Friday for sign-off. :rocket:

any final quick thoughts?

leo (tech-ops): include a short decision log entry when we override score for business reasons. keeps audit trail.

jessica (PM): good point — will add a required "override_reason" field for manual admits.

mira (ML): ok, sending a short PR with the eval thresholds end of day.

anya (product-ops): will draft onboarding checklist and share in #product by EOD Thursday.

sam (infra): thumbs up.

jessica (PM): thanks team — closing thread.
